title: Baker Hughes Posts Record $39.4B Backlog for Energy Technology Arm
summary:
The energy services company reported third-quarter revenue of $8B, topping the $7.7B projected by analysts, as it benefited from a surge in power generation requests for artificial intelligence data centers. Baker Hughes posted adjusted earnings per share of $0.70, surpassing the $0.61 estimate, though GAAP earnings per share were $0.41 and total profit for the quarter declined. Growth was driven in part by the acquisition of Chart and the performance of the Industrial & Energy Technology (IET) arm, which saw new orders rise 42% from a year ago to $5.9B.

The company raised its order outlook for the IET segment to more than $50B for the 2026 to 2028 period, citing a record segment backlog of $39.4B. Specific bookings included 43 gas turbine packages for 1.1 GW of power for a major US tech company and another 500 MW for other AI facilities. Overall quarterly orders grew 31% to $10.8B, with total free cash flow reaching $769M.

selectedTweets.text:
$ 5.9bn of new orders in one quarter and a lot of it is gas turbines for AI.

Baker Hughes reported Q3 results. 

Its Industrial & Energy Technology (IET) arm, which builds turbines, compressors and LNG equipment, booked $ 5.9bn of orders, up 42% from a year ago.

What’s in the order book?

-1.1 GW of power generation for a major US tech company, with 43 gas turbine packages

-About 500 MW more for AI data centres, with 18 Frame 5 turbines

-🚨A large LNG order from Venture Global for the Plaquemines expansion (this gives a new business on top of the LNG export)

The IET backlog hit a record $ 39.4bn, out of $ 46.4bn for the whole company.

Management raised its 2026-2028 IET order outlook to $ 50bn or more.

The headline numbers:

Revenue $ 8.0bn, up 14%, helped by the Chart acquisition

Adjusted EPS $0.70 vs $0.61 expected

Free cash flow $769m

GAAP EPS $0.41

Data centres need power every hour of the day. 

Grids can’t connect them fast enough, so tech companies are building their own gas plants on site.

That turns AI demand straight into gas demand, and into turbine orders.

The other half of the story is LNG. 

Every new export plant needs compressors.

I’ve been bullish on gas for AI data centres and LNG all year. 

This is that thesis showing up as orders and backlog.
